sections.content: You know *se* with a verb from B1 Unit 6: it says what is done without saying who does it. Here it describes how a whole society was organised. With a person as the object, the verb stays singular and takes the personal *a* (*se clasificaba a las personas*). With a thing, the verb agrees with it (*se pintaban las ropas*).

items.spanish: Se llamaba mestizo a una persona de origen español e indígena.
items.english: A person of Spanish and indigenous origin was called a mestizo.

items.spanish: En los registros de bautizos se anotaba el origen de cada familia.
items.english: In the baptism registers, the origin of each family was written down.

items.spanish: En los cuadros se pintaban la ropa y los oficios de cada casta.
items.english: In the paintings, the clothes and trades of each casta were painted.

items.spanish: En el siglo XVIII se hacían series de pinturas de castas.
items.english: In the 18th century, series of casta paintings were made.

sections.content: The imperfect (*se clasificaba*) fits a practice that went on for years; the preterite (*se hizo popular*) fits one change. Check the noun: *se anotaba el origen* (singular), *se pintaban los oficios* (plural), but with a person, *se clasificaba a las personas* stays singular.
